advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-ground `test_enumeration_completeness_...` on observable behavior (e.g. drive each classified mutating member through its 429 boundary) rather than grepping `def` names in the source under test, so a private-helper rename does not falsely fail it.
evidence: `out = subprocess.run(["git", "grep", "-nE", r"^(    )?def [_a-z]", "--", *files], ...)` in `_step0_names()` greps the source under test
`unaccounted = names - accounted` / `assert not unaccounted` asserts the set of `def` NAMES in the implementation, not any behavior
The grep target is executable SOURCE CODE (acli*.py), so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception (non-executable instruction artifacts only) does not apply
Four-Criterion (a): renaming a private helper (e.g. `_run` → `_run_subprocess`) or adding an unclassified private helper breaks the test with zero observable-behavior change
advisory.finding: `test_enumeration_completeness_every_step0_name_is_accounted_for` runs `git grep` over the source code under test (acli.py/acli_graph.py/acli_rest.py/acli_cli_ops.py) to extract `def` names and asserts each is in a hardcoded classification set — a source-grep/change-detector that breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (renaming or extracting a private helper) with no observable-behavior change.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the DC cross-check derive at least one operand from executed product code (or DC's actual enumerated set) instead of comparing two literal constants defined in the same test file.
evidence: `missing = _DC_SWEPT - _CLASSIFIED_MUTATING` / `assert not missing` compares two hardcoded sets both defined earlier in this test module (`_DC_SWEPT` at :425, `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING` at :428)
Inverted-trace: the assertion cannot fail for any change in Cloud transport code — only for an edit to the in-file literals themselves
Four-Criterion (d): regression-blindness — the test detects no regression in the specific 429/mutation behavior this diff introduces
advisory.finding: `test_dc_crosscheck_every_dc_swept_mutation_is_covered_on_cloud` asserts `_DC_SWEPT - _CLASSIFIED_MUTATING == set()`, where both `_DC_SWEPT` and `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING` are literal constants defined in the same test file — it exercises no product code and can only fail if someone edits those literals.
